question: Can Optimal Brain Surgeon compensation in the coordinate system of an existing low-rank factorization repair the retained singular values after truncation without iterative fine-tuning?

key_findings.claim: SVD-Surgeon projects a layer's quadratic loss model from weight space into the coordinates of the factorization's diagonal coefficients while holding both factor directions fixed.
key_findings.evidence: For theta=U diag(sigma) V^T and delta theta=U diag(delta sigma) V^T, contraction of the fourth-order weight Hessian yields a compact l-by-l matrix H-bar and the quadratic form one-half delta-sigma^T H-bar delta-sigma. Orthonormal U and V are not required.

key_findings.claim: The projected empirical-Fisher estimate can be assembled from diagonal entries of U-transpose times the per-sample weight gradient times V.
key_findings.evidence: Each projected gradient is diag(U^T G_n V), and H-bar is estimated as the average outer product of these vectors, avoiding explicit second derivatives in the implementation.

key_findings.claim: The paper incorrectly equates its empirical-Fisher matrix with the exact singular-coordinate loss Hessian.
key_findings.evidence: The exact projection in Equation 8 would equal the singular-coordinate Hessian when H is the true weight Hessian. Equations 10-12 replace H by an empirical outer product of per-sample gradients, which generally differs from the loss Hessian except under additional likelihood/modeling identities not stated here.

key_findings.claim: Given a chosen pruned set, the optimal retained-coefficient update under the estimated quadratic model has a closed form.
key_findings.evidence: With delta sigma_C=-sigma_C, minimizing over retained coordinates yields delta sigma_S=H-bar_SS inverse H-bar_SC sigma_C, followed in practice by damping and an update scale lambda.

key_findings.claim: The single-value OBS saliency does not itself solve joint subset selection under interactions among multiple pruned values.
key_findings.evidence: The select-and-update variant ranks individual scores sigma_i squared divided by twice the corresponding inverse-Hessian diagonal, then prunes the lowest. The joint loss for a set is instead a Schur-complement quadratic with off-diagonal interactions.

key_findings.claim: The method composes algebraically with SVD-LLM's nonorthogonal whitened factorization.
key_findings.evidence: SVD-LLM absorbs the inverse Cholesky whitening transform into the right factor, so V is nonorthogonal; SVD-Surgeon's derivation only assumes a fixed U diag(sigma) V^T factorization and therefore still applies.

key_findings.claim: Closed-form compensation sharply improves the whitening-only SVD-LLM truncation baseline at aggressive compression in the tested OPT models.
key_findings.evidence: At 70% compression on WikiText-2, OPT-6.7B perplexity falls from 944.57 for whitening-only SVD-LLM to 47.27 for update-only and 46.36 for select-and-update. This is not a comparison against SVD-LLM's full sequential LoRA recovery, and the gains are smaller under mild compression and for LLaMA-2-7B.

key_findings.claim: Most of the empirical gain comes from updating retained values, not the proposed saliency ranking.
key_findings.evidence: Across WikiText-2 and C4 tables, select-and-update generally improves only modestly over update-only and occasionally loses slightly, whereas both substantially outperform the host at high ratios.

key_findings.claim: The compression-time plot omits the dominant Fisher-assembly cost.
key_findings.evidence: The plotted runtime loads precomputed H-bar from disk. The paper separately reports about 7.6 seconds per calibration sample for LLaMA-2-7B and uses N=32,768 there, which is roughly 69 serial hours before parallelization, plus per-layer forward/backward work.

key_findings.claim: 'Training-free' means no iterative parameter optimization, not gradient-free or cheap calibration.
key_findings.evidence: The method requires 16,384-32,768 calibration samples, layerwise backward gradients, damping, block truncation, and model-specific manually explored compensation scales; these gradients build the one-shot closed-form update.

key_findings.claim: The broad plug-in claim is demonstrated on only one host ablation and is not compared with the full host recovery or contemporary loss-aware low-rank alternatives.
key_findings.evidence: All experiments layer the method on whitening-only SVD-LLM, excluding that host's sequential LoRA recovery. OBD-LLM is cited as a Hessian/K-FAC low-rank method but receives no matched comparison, and no ASVD, OBD-LLM, IO-SVD, or other host composition is tested.

key_findings.claim: The evaluation establishes perplexity recovery, not downstream capability or realized inference acceleration.
key_findings.evidence: Experiments cover WikiText-2 on four 1.3B-7B models and C4 on two OPT models; no downstream zero-shot tasks, generation quality, memory benchmark, kernel throughput, or end-to-end serving result is reported.

key_findings.claim: The method does not rescue the most aggressive LLaMA-2 or C4 settings even when it improves the selected baseline.
key_findings.evidence: At 70% and 80% compression, LLaMA-2-7B select-and-update perplexity is still 232.76 and 531.62 versus 5.47 dense. At 80% compression on C4, select-and-update remains at 2915.40 for OPT-1.3B and 3664.16 for OPT-2.7B.

method.core_idea: Treat the diagonal coefficients of any fixed low-rank factorization as the parameters in an Optimal Brain Surgeon problem, then compensate the retained coefficients after truncation using projected curvature.
method.mechanism: Per-sample weight gradients are projected to coefficient space, their empirical outer products form a damped compact curvature matrix, and a block linear solve updates retained coefficients. An optional individual OBS saliency reorders which coefficients to remove.
assumptions: The pretrained model lies close enough to a stationary point for a local second-order loss model to be useful.
Layerwise block diagonality and an empirical-Fisher approximation preserve the important loss interactions.
Holding U and V fixed leaves enough compensating capacity in sigma alone.
Damping, block truncation, sample count, and update scaling can stabilize the approximate solve.

techniques.role: Operates on the coefficients of an SVD-like factorization supplied by a host compressor.
Uses an OBS quadratic model to compensate parameters after pruning.
Approximates projected curvature with outer products of calibration gradients.
Solves a damped block linear system instead of iterative fine-tuning.

evaluations.setting: OPT-1.3B, 2.7B, and 6.7B plus LLaMA-2-7B on WikiText-2, 20%-80% compression
evaluations.result: Both variants improve whitening-only SVD-LLM at every reported ratio; the OPT gains become very large at 60%-80% compression, while LLaMA gains are modest and its 70%-80% perplexities remain extremely high.
evaluations.baseline: SVD-LLM truncation-aware whitening only, not the full sequential LoRA-recovery pipeline

evaluations.setting: OPT-1.3B and OPT-2.7B on C4, 20%-80% compression
evaluations.result: Compensation improves the host across ratios, with the clearest separation in the aggressive regime.
The closed-form update accounts for most recovery; individual saliency selection adds a small and inconsistent incremental change.
evaluations.baseline: Host-selected smallest coefficients versus OBS-saliency-selected coefficients

evaluations.metric: Seconds for truncation/update after loading precomputed curvature
evaluations.result: Update-only adds modest solve overhead and select-and-update costs more due to a larger pseudoinverse.
evaluations.baseline: SVD-LLM compression stage, excluding curvature assembly

limitations: Author-stated: evaluation is limited to perplexity on WikiText-2 and C4, one host compressor, and four model checkpoints.
Author-stated: U and V are frozen, so compensation cannot rotate the retained subspace.
Author-stated: empirical-Fisher collection requires expensive forward/backward calibration passes for every layer.
Author-stated: damping, update scale, truncation fraction, and sample count lack a principled selection rule.
Reviewer inference: empirical Fisher is not generally the exact loss Hessian despite the text's equality claim.
Reviewer inference: the runtime chart excludes curvature assembly, which dominates end-to-end compression cost at the stated sample counts.
Reviewer inference: only the whitening-only SVD-LLM ablation is tested, so host-agnostic composability is algebraic rather than empirically demonstrated and the full host recovery is not a baseline.
Reviewer inference: OBD-LLM, IO-SVD, Zero Sum SVD, and other close loss-aware low-rank methods are not included in matched comparisons.
Reviewer inference: no convergence or sensitivity study validates the stated 16,384-32,768 Fisher-sample requirement, block truncation, damping, or model-specific update scale.
Reviewer inference: no downstream accuracy, generation quality, memory, or realized inference-throughput evaluation is provided.
failure_modes: Empirical-Fisher curvature differs from true loss curvature and produces a misdirected or excessive compensation.
A poorly conditioned retained block requires damping that erases useful cross-coordinate information.
Fixed singular directions cannot represent the best post-truncation repair.
Independent saliency ranking chooses a jointly poor subset because pruned coefficients interact.
Manual update scaling transfers poorly across model families or calibration domains.
Calibration-gradient cost outweighs deployment savings for one-off or frequently changing models.
Perplexity recovery fails to translate into downstream capability or actual hardware speedup.
reusable_insights: Project curvature into the exact low-dimensional coordinates exposed by a compression factorization before attempting full weight-space surgery.
Separate subset selection from survivor compensation; the latter can deliver most of the gain even with an unchanged pruning rule.
Report curvature-collection time, storage, and backward passes separately from the final closed-form solve.
Use 'training-free' narrowly and quantify calibration gradients so it is not mistaken for data- or backward-free compression.
Validate empirical-Fisher curvature against Hessian-vector or held-out loss changes before calling it exact second order.
Test host-agnostic claims by composing with multiple factorizations, especially a close curvature-aware host.
open_questions: Does the compensation remain beneficial on OBD-LLM, ASVD, or other nonorthogonal low-rank hosts?
Can a K-FAC, generalized Gauss-Newton, or Hessian-vector approximation improve fidelity with fewer than tens of thousands of gradients?
Can joint subset selection exploit the Schur-complement interactions without a combinatorial search?
Are limited rotations of U and V worth their additional curvature and optimization cost?
How does recovered perplexity translate to zero-shot tasks, long-context behavior, generation, memory, and wall-clock inference?
Can damping and update scale be chosen from held-out predicted-versus-realized loss rather than manual per-model exploration?

competitive_landscape.title: SVD-LLM: Truncation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Large Language Model Compression
competitive_landscape.relationship: The direct host and experimental baseline; it whitens activations so coefficient magnitude aligns with layer reconstruction loss and provides post-truncation recovery.
competitive_landscape.difference: SVD-Surgeon leaves the host factorization fixed and applies task-loss empirical-Fisher OBS compensation to retained coefficients; its comparison excludes SVD-LLM's iterative LoRA-style recovery.

competitive_landscape.title: Optimal Brain Decomposition for Accurate LLM Low-Rank Approximation
competitive_landscape.relationship: The closest second-order low-rank competitor; uses task-loss Hessian structure to derive bidirectional whitening and a closed-form decomposition.
competitive_landscape.difference: OBD-LLM changes how the low-rank factors are formed using K-FAC input/output curvature, while SVD-Surgeon performs OBS repair in the coefficient basis of an already chosen host factorization.

competitive_landscape.title: IO-SVD: Input-Output Whitened SVD for Adaptive-Rank LLM Compression
competitive_landscape.relationship: A contemporary loss-aware SVD competitor that combines input whitening with an output metric from a second-order KL expansion and globally allocates heterogeneous ranks.
competitive_landscape.difference: IO-SVD changes the factorization metric and rank allocation before truncation, whereas SVD-Surgeon projects per-sample task gradients into a fixed host coefficient basis and repairs only the retained coefficients afterward.

competitive_landscape.title: Zero Sum SVD: Balancing Loss Sensitivity for Low Rank LLM Compression
competitive_landscape.relationship: A close post-training competitor that uses activation whitening, first-order calibration-loss estimates, global component selection, and an optional single projected-gradient correction.
competitive_landscape.difference: Zero Sum SVD optimizes cross-layer selection and optionally updates/retruncates weights using first-order information; SVD-Surgeon uses an OBS block solve to compensate retained coefficients within each already selected factorization.

competitive_landscape.title: SigmaScale: LLM Compression with SVD-based Low-Rank Decomposition and Learned Scaling Matrices
competitive_landscape.relationship: A near-contemporaneous SVD compressor that learns diagonal row and column scalings under an activation-aware reconstruction loss before truncation.
competitive_landscape.difference: SigmaScale iteratively learns a more compressible coordinate system and then decomposes it; SVD-Surgeon accepts a fixed host coordinate system and applies a closed-form task-gradient compensation after pruning.

competitive_landscape.title: The LLM Surgeon
competitive_landscape.relationship: Scales curvature-aware surgery and survivor updates to structured and unstructured LLM pruning.
competitive_landscape.difference: It uses Kronecker-factored weight-space curvature to remove rows, columns, or weights; SVD-Surgeon reduces the problem to diagonal factor coefficients and targets dense low-rank deployment.

competitive_landscape.title: ASVD: Activation-aware Singular Value Decomposition for Compressing Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: A training-free low-rank compressor that rescales weights using activation statistics and allocates layer-specific ranks.
competitive_landscape.difference: ASVD makes the decomposition activation-aware and includes iterative calibration; SVD-Surgeon uses per-sample task-loss gradients to repair retained coefficients after a host truncation.

competitive_landscape.title: Language model compression with weighted low-rank factorization
competitive_landscape.relationship: An earlier Fisher-aware low-rank method that weights reconstruction errors by parameter importance before factorization.
competitive_landscape.difference: Fisher-Weighted SVD uses importance weighting to form the low-rank approximation for task-specific language models; SVD-Surgeon instead estimates a compact full coefficient covariance and solves for survivor compensation after a host truncation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first application of Optimal Brain Surgeon directly in singular-value coordinates, yielding plug-in closed-form survivor updates and saliency for arbitrary fixed factorizations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The derivation reduces an exact weight Hessian to coefficient space without requiring orthogonal factors, then instantiates an empirical-Fisher approximation and demonstrates large high-compression recovery on the whitening-only SVD-LLM host.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Coefficient-space OBS survivor compensation is a clean, plausibly distinct contribution, and the update—not the individual saliency ranking—drives most of the reported gain. Novelty is narrower than the broad second-order-compression framing because SVD-LLM already has iterative recovery, FWSVD already injects Fisher importance, and OBD-LLM, IO-SVD, and Zero Sum SVD are close loss-aware alternatives; only one host ablation is tested, and the empirical-Fisher/exact-Hessian language is incorrect.

verification.passage_check: Re-read all 11 pages of the pinned arXiv v1 PDF and rechecked every finding against Equations 3-22, the exact-Hessian/Fisher transition in Equations 8 and 10-12, the Schur-complement and single-value saliency in Equations 18-20, Tables 1-5, Figure 2's timing definition, the limitations, and both appendix pages. Numeric transcriptions for OPT, LLaMA-2, C4, sample counts, damping, and the 7.6-second per-sample statement were independently recomputed or visually checked.
verification.competitor_check: Independently checked official current primary records and exact versions for SVD-LLM 2403.07378v5, OBD-LLM 2604.00821v1, IO-SVD 2605.15626v1, Zero Sum SVD 2602.02848v1, SigmaScale 2606.07098v1, ASVD 2312.05821v5, FWSVD 2207.00112v1, and the ICLR 2024 OpenReview record for The LLM Surgeon; the target was excluded and all URLs, titles, methodological distinctions, and self/duplicate constraints were rechecked on 2026-08-23.

reviewer_notes: Completed an independent secondary pass over all 11 cached pages, including the derivation, every table/figure, exact timing exclusion, hyperparameter tables, and three-seed OPT appendix. The local source is current arXiv v1. The exact projection of a true Hessian is valid, but Equation 12 is an empirical-Fisher surrogate and therefore not generally the exact singular-coordinate loss Hessian. The roughly 69-hour number is transparent serial-equivalent arithmetic from 7.6 seconds times 32,768, not measured wall clock and not a denial of the stated parallelism. The official implementation was also inspected for audit context, but no execution-level reproduction was attempted. Eight current, version-pinned primary competitors were checked; the comparison weakness is stronger than the primary reading stated because the experiment uses whitening-only SVD-LLM rather than its full recovery pipeline.
